name: hermes

soul_md.note: Hermes's default identity file (identity slot 1 of agent/prompt_builder.py), written into HERMES_HOME on Hermes's first run and byte-identical to /opt/harness/src/SOUL.md and /root/.hermes/SOUL.md in the harness image; the gbrain image build fetches it at this commit and checks the sha256, and gbrain/build-install.ts seeds the hermes installer's HERMES_HOME with it before gbrain setup hermes --instructions-only, because gbrain appends its brain-first block to an existing SOUL.md and writes nothing into an empty HERMES_HOME (GBRA-188)

install: git clone --branch v2026.9.24 <repo> /opt/harness/src && uv venv /opt/harness/venv && uv pip install '/opt/harness/src[anthropic,mcp]'

model_openai.model: the cell's model from HE_MODEL_NAME (gpt-6-luna in the pilot); --provider openai-api --model <HE_MODEL_NAME> on every turn
model_openai.route: POST <HE_MODEL_BASE_URL>/v1/responses, streamed (SSE), through the OpenAI SDK
model_openai.selected_when: HE_MODEL_BASE_URL ends in /openai, the provider segment of the runner's <proxy>/<slot>/<provider> (runner/trial/proxy.ts baseUrlFor); any other URL keeps config/config.yaml, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL and --provider anthropic byte for byte (tests/openai-branch.test.ts golden captures from c1c7ed1b3)
model_openai.provider_name: openai-api is Hermes's direct OpenAI API-key provider (the hermes_cli/auth.py registry row; transport codex_responses and base_url_env_var OPENAI_BASE_URL in hermes_cli/providers.py HERMES_OVERLAYS); `--provider openai` would resolve to openrouter, the legacy alias in hermes_cli/providers.py _ALIAS_GROUPS
model_openai.reasoning_setting: agent.reasoning_effort: medium in config.openai.yaml, sent on the agent's turn as reasoning {effort: medium, summary: auto}; Hermes's own default sends the same. The one-shot title call (auxiliary.title_generation, provider auto = the main model) sends reasoning {effort: none} with no tools, as Hermes ships it
model_openai.auxiliary_models: every auxiliary task defaults to provider auto, the main model (hermes_cli/config_defaults.py auxiliary; title_generation.prefer_fast_model false), so side calls name the cell model; observed: the title call named gpt-6-luna
model_openai.max_output_tokens: none stated: on the openai-api provider Hermes sends no output cap, so the proxy writes its own (observed 2026-10-29 through the lease-mode proxy: at --max-output-tokens 100000 the request upstream carried 100000, at 128000 it carried 128000; the 32768 recorded before was the proxy's default filled in). Every shard runs --max-output-tokens 128000, so each request reserves 128000 output tokens
model_openai.shipped_defaults: everything else is Hermes's: model metadata from its catalog (context 1,050,000 for gpt-6-luna, logged as a hardcoded catalog match for a custom endpoint), the Responses transport, retries and tools
model_openai.rig_limitation: Hermes classes the proxy host (host.docker.internal) as a local model server (agent/model_metadata.py is_local_endpoint) and probes it for a local server's metadata: GET /api/v1/models, /api/tags, /v1/props, /props, /version, /models and POST /api/show, which the proxy refuses 403 with no model at $0, and GET /v1/models and /v1/models/<model>, which it forwards as free metadata reads. The same probes are refused on an Anthropic cell; no setting turns them off at this pin. They carry no model field, so HE-MODEL-001 does not count them (docs/errors.md). GET /v1/models/<model> is sent for the cell model and for model.default, so the adapter writes the cell model into model.default (HARN-20; before that the templates' claude-sonnet-5-5 and gpt-6-luna showed up in that path)
model_openai.observed_keyless: 2026-10-29, image harness-eval/hermes built at c1c7ed1b3 with the checkout's adapter, config/ and pin.json mounted, through runner/proxy/metering-proxy.ts in lease mode (--allow-models openai:gpt-6-luna, --upstream openai=<fake Responses endpoint, tests/fixtures/openai-branch/fake-openai.ts>, placeholder upstream key, a slot bound with a per-trial token): run completed with exit 0 on two POST /v1/responses naming gpt-6-luna (the title call and the agent turn), serve with exit 0 on one, all forwarded and priced, no refused line that names a model, only the metadata probes above refused, and the fake saw only the proxy's placeholder key; a cell model off the allowlist (gpt-6.1-sol) was refused 403 and the adapter exited 3 (tests/openai-branch.test.ts)

model_particle.model: the cell's model from HE_MODEL_NAME (particle-1); --provider custom:particle --model particle-1 on every turn
model_particle.route: POST <HE_MODEL_BASE_URL>/v1/chat/completions through the OpenAI SDK: the agent turn streamed with stream_options.include_usage, the one-shot title call not streamed
model_particle.base_url_env: OPENAI_BASE_URL (set from HE_MODEL_BASE_URL + /v1), expanded into model.base_url and custom_providers[particle].base_url
model_particle.api_key_env: OPENAI_API_KEY (set from HE_MODEL_API_KEY), named by custom_providers[particle].key_env; no ANTHROPIC_* variable is set
model_particle.selected_when: HE_MODEL_BASE_URL ends in /particle, the provider segment of the runner's <proxy>/<slot>/<provider> for a particle:particle-1 cell (runner/trial/proxy.ts baseUrlFor); an Anthropic or OpenAI URL keeps its config, variables and --provider (tests/particle-branch.test.ts)
model_particle.provider_name: custom:particle is the custom_providers entry named particle (hermes_cli/providers.py resolve_custom_provider and custom_provider_slug at the pinned commit), a user-config provider on transport openai_chat, which determine_api_mode maps to chat_completions for a host that mandates no other mode. openai-api would use the Responses transport, which Particle serves only over WebSocket
model_particle.reasoning_setting: custom_providers[particle].extra_body reasoning_effort medium, which the OpenAI SDK sends as a top-level field. On a custom endpoint Hermes sends no reasoning field of its own (agent/reasoning_params.py _supports_reasoning_extra_body is false for an unknown host), which Particle would serve at its default high tier; medium names the same tier explicitly, as every harness on the cell sends medium (plan decision 6). Observed reasoning_effort medium on the agent turn
model_particle.auxiliary_models: every auxiliary task defaults to provider auto, the main model (hermes_cli/config_defaults.py auxiliary), so side calls name particle-1. The run entry's one-shot title call sends reasoning_effort none, no tools and no output cap, and does not carry extra_body, as Hermes ships it; with none Particle does not think, so its default cap of 32000 is ample. The serve entry made no side call
model_particle.max_output_tokens_note: custom_providers[particle].extra_body max_completion_tokens 128000 on the agent turn: Hermes states no cap of its own on a custom endpoint (it has no config setting for the main agent's cap at this pin), and Particle spends output on reasoning_content first. 128000 is the cap the OpenAI cells run under (the proxy fills it there) and every shard's proxy runs; the title call states none, so the proxy fills its cap
model_particle.error_mapping: the same model-error pattern as every cell: a provider 400 is exit 2 (Hermes prints it as HTTP 400 and does not retry it), a 402 or 429 exit 3. Plan decision 12 (a 400 with code invalid_value or unsupported_parameter is model_error) is applied by the runner from the metering proxy record; Hermes drops error.code from its output (agent/api_error_summary.py)
model_particle.rig_limitation: as on an OpenAI cell (model_openai.rig_limitation), Hermes classes the endpoint host as a local model server and probes it for metadata: GET /api/v1/models, /api/tags, /v1/props, /props, /version, /v1/models, /models, /v1/models/particle-1 and POST /api/show. None names a model
model_particle.shipped_defaults: everything else is Hermes's: the chat_completions transport, model metadata, retries and tools
model_particle.observed_keyless: 2026-10-31, image harness-eval/hermes built from this checkout with its adapter, config/ and pin.json mounted, straight against tests/fixtures/particle/fake-particle.ts at <fake>/<slot>/particle (the proxy's Particle route was not on main yet): run completed with exit 0 on two POST <base>/v1/chat/completions naming particle-1 (the agent turn: stream true, include_usage true, reasoning_effort medium, max_completion_tokens 128000, 23 tools; the title call: reasoning_effort none, no cap), serve with exit 0 on one agent turn of the same shape, besides the metadata probes; no /v1/embeddings and no Anthropic request, and every chat request carried the per-trial placeholder token; with the fake answering Particle error bodies (code in its own field) 400, 402 and 429, the run exited 2, 3 and 3 (tests/particle-branch.test.ts)

mcp_config_path: /harness-state/hermes/config.yaml#mcp_servers.world (appended at serve start: url HE_WORLD_MCP_URL, headers.Authorization: Bearer HE_WORLD_MCP_TOKEN; tools register as mcp__world__<tool>; the image installs the `mcp` extra so the client SDK is present)
multi_user_mode: CLI with one named session per conversation (dm:<member>, channel:<id>) in one HERMES_HOME; the gateway and its per-user sessions are not used

serve.session_key: dm:<member> | channel:<id> (session title; hermes chat -c <title> --create-if-missing); :t<thread_ts> appended when TurnRequest.thread_ts is set (a task turn with thread = "new" opens a new session in the same conversation)
serve.shared_between_sessions: whatever Hermes's own memory shares across sessions; not configured by the adapter
serve.reply_source: stream-json terminal `result` record (text, exit_code, error, tokens)
serve.exit_mapping: hermes exit 0 -> 0; outer timeout -> 124; proxy refusal, Anthropic SDK error class or HTTP status on stderr or in the result -> 3; else 2

gbrain_mcp: with HE_GBRAIN_MCP_URL and HE_GBRAIN_MCP_TOKEN set at serve start, an mcp_servers.gbrain block (url, headers.Authorization: Bearer <token>, timeout 120, connect_timeout 60) is appended beside world in /harness-state/hermes/config.yaml; tools register as mcp__gbrain__<tool>; `hermes mcp list` is logged. Unset, the config is byte-identical to a cell without gbrain

gbrain_install.variables: HE_GBRAIN_INSTALL=gbrain-docs with HE_GBRAIN_SPLIT (dev | heldout) and HE_GBRAIN_INSTALL_DIR (/he-gbrain-install, the exported view mounted read-only by the runner); the install ladder's docs rungs (docs/gbrain-arm.md)
source_commands: gbrain skillpack scaffold --all --workspace /workspace (gbrain INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md step 5, 'cd <workspace> && gbrain skillpack scaffold --all'; the workspace is explicit because the cd form does not resolve an empty directory at the pin)

gbrain compile-context --target hermes --include-core --out .hermes.md against the split's bot-visible brain (gbrain docs/mcp/HERMES.md 'Always-loaded core memory': the project context file Hermes reads; the docs write it at the git root, which for a trial workspace with no repository is the cwd)
gbrain_install.applied_by: adapter.sh before the harness is prepared (before the world-MCP wiring and ready): the manifest must name this harness and HE_GBRAIN_SPLIT and its view_digest must match its file list; every listed file is checked against its sha256, copied from <view>/workspace/<x> to /workspace/<x> (skills/ at the pinned gbrain commit, the full bundle of 64 skills in 127 files) and <view>/.hermes.md to /workspace/.hermes.md (dev 18 pages, held-out 25) and checked again; an existing destination is refused as skillpack scaffold refuses to overwrite
gbrain_install.record: $HE_LOG_DIR/gbrain-install.json (status, code, harness, split, dir, view_digest, files, destinations, copied, error) and ready.gbrain_install {status, files, view_digest, destinations}; ready.adapter_sha256 is the sha256 of the adapter file that ran
gbrain_install.failure: HE-ADAPTER-006, exit 2 before ready, the code and reason in gbrain-install.json and adapter.log

loaded_by_harness..hermes.md: yes: Hermes v2026.9.24 agent/prompt_builder.py build_context_files_prompt (lines 1733-1759) loads one project context file, first match wins, .hermes.md/HERMES.md before AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and .cursorrules; _find_hermes_md (lines 139-148) looks in the cwd and, only inside a git repository, its parents up to the root, so in /workspace (no repository) it reads /workspace/.hermes.md exactly. The cwd is terminal.cwd from config/config.yaml (/workspace) through agent/runtime_cwd.py resolve_context_cwd (line 105), else the process cwd, and the adapter runs hermes from /workspace. The content is injection-scanned (_scan_context_content, line 81: a match blocks the file) and capped by context_file_max_chars (hermes_cli/config_defaults.py line 498, null scales with the context window, floor 20K chars). hermes chat does not set skip_context_files (only --ignore-rules does, hermes_cli/main.py line 1822). Observed keylessly in the image after the install: build_context_files_prompt(cwd='/workspace') returns '# Project Context' with a '## .hermes.md' section holding every kept page heading of the dev view, 2889 chars, nothing blocked (tests/adapter-install.test.ts)
loaded_by_harness.skills: no: Hermes reads skills from HERMES_HOME/skills (/harness-state/hermes/skills; hermes_constants.py get_skills_dir, line 1473), skills.external_dirs (agent/skill_utils.py get_external_skills_dirs, line 359) and, for a project, only <git root>/.hermes/skills or <git root>/.agents/skills when that root is in skills.trusted_project_dirs (agent/skill_utils.py lines 431-437, _candidate_project_skills_dirs line 495 and get_project_skills_dirs line 517; get_all_skills_dirs, line 420, excludes project dirs). /workspace/skills is none of these and /workspace has no git root, so the scaffolded skills are copied as documented and not loaded. Observed keylessly: get_all_skills_dirs() is ['/harness-state/hermes/skills'] and get_project_skills_dirs() is [] with the skills in place (tests/adapter-install.test.ts)

gbrain_install.unset: with HE_GBRAIN_INSTALL unset nothing of this runs; the only difference from a cell without it is the adapter_sha256 field every ready file now carries

internal_network: serves on network "internal" on a gpt-6-luna cell, the same-model control for Codex (tests/internal-network-harnesses.test.ts, 2026-10-29): one turn through the lease-mode proxy with a world-MCP post_message landed through tool_call (on this provider Hermes defers MCP tools behind tool_search); from inside the container the proxy port connects and 1.1.1.1:443 and chatgpt.com:443 fail. Without security.allow_lazy_installs: false Hermes tried to lazy-install boto3 (provider.bedrock) and edge-tts from pypi.org during the turn, about 30 s until DNS failed each time, and the turn took 60 to 110 s against a fake that answers at once; both configs now set it (exists at this pin, hermes_cli/config_defaults.py, read by tools/lazy_deps.py), and the same test turn takes about 12 s. until HARN-18 (H10 PR 2) Hermes still tried to download the tirith scanner, which failed there and fell back to pattern matching; the image now carries the pinned scanner (tirith below), so no download is tried. security.tirith_enabled stays on because turning it off changes how Hermes gates dangerous commands

tirith.source: https://github.com/sheeki03/tirith/releases/tag/v0.4.2 (published 2026-09-11, the latest release on 2026-11-01 and so the one Hermes's unpinned download fetched where the network allowed)
tirith.install: Dockerfile: the release archive for the build's TARGETARCH, checked against archive_sha256 (the values in the release's checksums.txt), unpacked to /opt/tirith/bin, and tirith --version must print tirith 0.4.2
tirith.no_trial_download: TIRITH_BIN is an explicit path, which Hermes treats as authoritative and never replaces with a download (tools/tirith_security.py _resolve_locally: 'An explicit (non-"tirith") path is authoritative: never auto-download a replacement'; the env var wins over security.tirith_path in _load_security_config). TIRITH_OFFLINE=1 makes Tirith's own background threat-DB update a no-op and its runtime threat lookups cache-only (crates/tirith/src/cli/threatdb_cmd.rs maybe_background_update, check.rs), so no cell downloads threat data and the verdicts depend on the binary alone
tirith.how_hermes_uses_it: every terminal command in a serve turn is a single-query session (hermes chat --oneshot sets HERMES_SINGLE_QUERY_SESSION=1), so approvals.single_query_mode (Hermes's default deny; the adapter writes no approvals: block) decides it with no card: the dangerous-command patterns first, then tirith check --json --non-interactive --shell posix, and a Tirith block or warn blocks the command (tools/approval.py _unattended_deny). MCP tool calls, gbrain's included, never pass this gate
tirith.behavior_change: HARN-18 (H10 PR 2): before this pin the counted Hermes image had no Tirith; on the internal network the download failed and Hermes gated commands by pattern matching only (README 'Behavior changes'). Every Hermes cell from this image runs the scanner on the agent's own terminal commands
tirith.receipt: route cells record the effective approval mode, the Tirith path, version, sha256 and whether it matches binary_sha256 in $HE_LOG_DIR/hermes-security.json and ready.instruction_route (approvals, tirith), and every approval card or blocked command per turn in turns/<turn>.security.json
